text:
jess: quick heads-up 3 ran an onboarding pass for mynest-v1 -> mynest-v1-quant5 (5-bit per-channel symmetric) on multilingual holdouts (en/es/ja). seeing odd behavior: recall@1 stable, recall@5 down ~3pts, and cluster cohesion (DB index) worse. any ideas? :confused:

anya: do you have the eval config & numbers?

jess: short paste below:

```
model: mynest-v1-quant5
holdouts: en/es/ja (5k each)
metrics:
  recall@1: 0.69 -> 0.69
  recall@5: 0.86 -> 0.83
  recall@10: 0.92 -> 0.90
  db_index (lower is better): v1=0.38 -> v2=0.47
  idflip: 0.3% -> 1.8%
calib: 1500 random pooled
whitening: disabled (weird interactions in ja)
batching: 16
```

siva: idflip and DB index both moving suggests quantization noise increasing intra-cluster spread. 5-bit is aggressive; are you using outlier clipping or percentile-based calib?

jess: percentile 99.9 clipping, no stratification. ja appears to be hit hardest; long tail tokens in japanese cause some channels to have extremely low activations.

mike: can you run a quick per-lang calibration (separate scales per lang) and also an L2-normalized run? might isolate whether language-specific activation distributions are collapsing.

jess: started two runs: (A) per-lang calib (n=1000 each) (B) global post-L2-normalize across dims. queued.

eval-bot: run 1766011111 queued. full per-cluster files will be available at internal.eval/1766011111 when complete.

anya: another angle: kNN index config could interact—if index PQ/quantization combos are tuned for high-dim float behaviors, switching to aggressive embedding quant may widen distances non-uniformly. confirm the index metrics (ef/search) stayed constant.

jess: ef/search unchanged. this run used HNSW with PQ fallback.

siva: also look at per-dimension kurtosis / sparsity pre vs post quant. rare-language features often have skewed distributions; symmetric per-channel quant can underrepresent asymmetric activations. suggest trying asymmetric per-channel for channels with skew>3.

jess: good call. i'll add a selective asymmetric run for flagged channels where skew>3 and activation count < 1000 in calibration sample.

mike: and add a synthetic longtail probe to the eval harness: generate queries biased to low-frequency tokens and ensure recall@k doesn't drop >1.5pts. that will prevent regression sneaks.

jess: mini-update: per-lang calib micro-run (1k each) recovered recall@5 by ~1.5pts on ja and lowered idflip to 0.9%. L2-normalize run recovered ~0.5pts but DB index still worse on some clusters.

anya: sounds like both magnitude and angular distortion at play. prioritize per-lang calib + selective asymmetric for the worst channels. if that fixes, we can ship a config change rather than revert quant level.

jess: plan: 1) full per-lang calibration (5k each) 2) selective asymmetric-per-channel experiment on flagged dims 3) add synthetic longtail regression test to the CI eval-bot 4) if green, PR to quant pipeline to enable per-lang calib for multilingual tables and the selective asymmetric fallback. will post links here. :thumbsup:

siva: ping me to review the per-dim skew code.

mike: nice. if you want i can prototype the synthetic generator later today.

jess: thanks everyone, updating once full runs finish (~35m). :coffee:
